text.p: Portuguese bonds rose in brisk trade, boosted the Federal Reserve's decision not to raise U.S. short-term rates.
Dealers said the 10-year yield spread with Bunds would consolidate at just below 60 basis points while short and medium bond prices would make further gains during the session.

"The Fed opted for no change and foreign markets are buoyant which is driving our futures higher and lending support to the whole yield curve. We could reach new highs today," said one director of fixed-rate debt.
"Ten-year bonds will consolidate at just under 60 basis points with Bunds but this could go to 55 if Spain maintains its strong performance," said another trader.
"The real strength lies in five-year maturities. The yield curve is bound to get steeper today," he said.
Some dealers thought the strength of shorter maturities would prompt the Bank of Portugal to cut its rates soon.
June futures, which broke through resistance at 109.50, found a new ceiling at between 110.0 and 110.25.
